title: Generational Trends: A Playbook for Financial Institutions
summary: 2026 generational banking trends show how financial institutions can build digital experiences that create clarity, coordination, control, and protection.
body_markdown:
## How banks and credit unions can make digital experiences more relevant at every life stage


The traditional definition of primacy is being challenged as we know it as consumers continue to expand their financial relationships for niche needs. The market is crowded. Megabanks have scale, neobanks move quickly, artificial intelligence (AI) is drastically shifting consumer habits, and big technology (tech) platforms have trained people to expect intuitive, predictive, data-powered experiences.


The financial institutions that stay central to the banking relationship will be those that understand the moment – when to simplify, guide, protect, and offer the next best step. Regional and community financial institutions have deep relationship advantages, but those advantages need to show up digitally.


### Economic influencers impacting generations


Before jumping into the findings from the[2026 Generational Trends in Digital Banking Report](https://www.alkami.com/resources/research/2026-generational-trends-in-digital-banking-report/) , let’s explore the societal and economic influences that are impacting each generation’s banking preferences.


**Generation Z (Gen Z)**


AI is reshaping the U.S. job market, creating a divergence between roles where AI acts as a force multiplier for output and roles where AI makes the job easier.


[Jobs requiring specific AI skills are growing almost eight times (69%) faster than the total jobs market (9%)](https://www.pwc.com/gx/en/news-room/press-releases/2026/pwc-2026-ai-jobs-barometer.html?utm_source=chatgpt.com) , and entry-level roles now require more tenured experience, like judgment and leadership. However, many recent graduates are facing an AI skills gap with


[nearly half of college students saying their programs had not meaningfully integrated AI](https://www.marketwatch.com/story/teachers-ban-it-employers-demand-it-new-grads-face-a-frustrating-ai-double-standard-09c70f19?utm_source=chatgpt.com) . These pressures are changing how Gen Z approaches work and financial decisions.


[Fifty-five percent of Gen Z say they have delayed major life decisions](https://www.deloitte.com/na/en/about/press-room/deloitte-2026-gen-z-and-millennial-survey.html?utm_source=chatgpt.com) , such as starting a family, pursuing further education, or launching a business, because of their finances. This suggests a need for clear, confidence-building guidance and a trusted financial partner.


**Millennials**


Similar to Gen Z, more millennials are[diverging from traditional timelines than previous generations due to their financial situation (52%)](https://www.deloitte.com/global/en/issues/work/genz-millennial-survey.html?utm_source=chatgpt.com) . While many millennials are also exposed to “sandwich generation” pressure, meaning they have a child under 18 and a living parent. A[2026 article](https://www.care.com/c/sandwich-generation-caregiver-report/?utm_source=chatgpt.com) found that among “sandwich generation” Americans, 82% say caregiving costs have left their household financially strained, 77% feel financially behind, and 52% say caregiving has pushed savings to the back burner. Among millennial caregivers, 61% have turned down a promotion, raise or other opportunity because of their caregiving responsibilities.


**Generation X (Gen X)**


Gen X is also a member of the “sandwich generation” and is actively managing several expensive life stages at once – raising children, helping with college costs, caring for aging parents, and preparing for retirement – making visibility and control especially important. Families spent an average of[$34,019 on college for the 2025-2026 academic year, up 10% from the prior year](https://www.salliemae.com/about/leading-research/how-america-pays-for-college/) . At the same time,[only 49% of Gen Xers believe they will be financially ready for retirement](https://news.northwesternmutual.com/planning-and-progress-study-2026) . Gen X is carrying significant financial responsibility with limited room for error.


**Baby Boomers**


While security is top of mind across generations, fraud risk is especially prevalent for Baby Boomers.[Victims over age 60 filed more than 201,000 complaints in 2025 and reported losses of more than $7.7 billion](https://www.fbi.gov/news/stories/scammers-target-older-adult-victims) . A[Federal Trade Commission’s report](https://www.ftc.gov/news-events/news/press-releases/2025/12/ftc-issues-annual-report-congress-agencys-actions-protect-older-adults) found a dramatic increase in older adults reporting fraud losses of $100,000+ from 2020 to 2024, rising from about $600 million to $2.4 billion – driven largely by major losses from a variety of investment, romance, and impersonation scams.


### A generation-by-generation playbook for financial institutions


Now that we have some generational context of what’s happening in the world, it’s time to turn these insights into action. The strongest generational strategy starts with what each generation is trying to accomplish and designs the connected banking journey around those needs.


### Gen Z: build clarity


Gen Z Insights


- 81% say their financial institution’s ability to understand their financial goals is important or very important to them.
- 57% look to their primary provider for financial education.
- 33% plan to grow the number of companies they have a financial relationship with in the next year; the highest of any generation.


Takeaway for Financial Institutions


- Make[digital account opening](https://www.alkami.com/digital-banking-solutions/retail-banking/digital-account-opening/) fast, mobile-first, and confidence-building.
- Use referral strategies and relationship-building offers.
- Offer practical, step-by-step financial education.
- Use AI-enabled guidance, but explain the value clearly.
- Deliver personalized offers in mobile and online banking.
- Show community impact in specific, local ways.


Gen Z is hungry for financial education and open to artificial intelligence (AI) if it improves the digital banking experience. The financial institution that helps them understand money early has a better chance to shape long-term habits. **Millennials: create coordination**


### Millennials: create coordination


Millennial Insights


- 77% prefer using their mobile device when opening a checking or savings account online.
- 65% feel comfortable with AI-enabled experiences that help them navigate spending, security, and everyday money management.
- 71% say the provider’s pace in bringing new helpful products is important to them.


Takeaway for Financial Institutions


- Use mobile-first personalized guidance.
- Connect budgeting, savings, debt, credit, and planning tools.
- Use behavioral data to anticipate next needs.
- Automate savings and cash-flow nudges.
- Make it easier to consolidate relationships.
- Offer[financial wellness](https://www.alkami.com/digital-banking-solutions/retail-banking/financial-wellness/) tools that reduce decision fatigue.


Millennials are carrying peak-life complexity. They are digitally fluent, receptive to AI-enabled tools, responsive to personalized offers, and likely need help navigating diverse financial scenarios. Millennials seek experiences that connect the dots.


### Gen X: provide control


Gen X Insights


- 63% prefer using their mobile device when opening a checking or savings account online.
- 91% say support via phone is very important or important to them, followed by 87% prioritizing online virtual assistance.
- 78% would feel comfortable with their financial institution using AI to alert them about suspected fraud and provide actionable next steps.


Takeaway for Financial Institutions


- Make digital banking a control center.
- Prioritize visibility, alerts, documentation, and easy[money movement](https://www.alkami.com/digital-banking-solutions/retail-banking/money-movement/) .
- Offer tools for family banking, college planning, debt, retirement, investing, and elder care.
- Pair digital convenience with knowledgeable support.
- Use AI-enabled alerts, fraud detection, and simplified decision support.


Gen X needs control as they manage childcare, college tuitions, caring for aging parents, managing housing costs, and trying to protect retirement. Convenience matters because their time, attention, and financial margin are already stretched.


### Baby Boomers: reinforce protection


Baby Boomer Insights


- 57% say access to knowledgeable staff matters most during a branch visit.
- 97% say that protecting their data from fraudsters and unauthorized third-parties is very important or important to their digital banking experience.
- 51% would be most likely to open a new account with their primary financial institution if the process took five minutes or less; significantly higher than younger generations.


Takeaway for Financial Institutions


- Emphasize security, privacy, and fraud protection.
- Avoid forcing channel migration.
- Make digital experiences clear, simple, and supported.
- Use AI first for protection, not prediction.
- Support trusted contacts, beneficiary updates, legacy planning, and scam education.
- Make it easy to reach human help.


Baby Boomers are wealth stewards and have a protection-first mindset; valuing tenure, familiarity, knowledgeable support, and confidence. Digital banking should help them preserve independence, protect assets, and make confident decisions about what comes next.

### Putting the pieces together


While generational signals can be helpful in understanding who might be entering or interacting with your financial institution and what their preferences are, generations are not a monolith. Ultimately, across all generations of account holders, 85% say digital experience quality is essential or important when considering a new primary provider.


Account opening is often the first meaningful test. Setting a tone that tells the account holder whether the financial institution is easy to work with and if the experience feels safe. Financial institutions that make account opening fast, secure, and intuitive can turn interest into momentum before a competitor does. Yet there is still room to improve the first digital interaction across all types of financial institutions – from megabanks to community financial institutions – with the average time to open a new account digitally being **7.4 minutes.** **** **** **** **** **** **** **** **** **** **** **** **** ****


Once onboarded, digital banking is where the relationship is experienced most frequently. A Gen Z consumer checking an account balance before a rent payment does not have the same expectations as a millennial managing household cash flow, a Gen Xer paying for college while also planning their retirement, or a Baby Boomer evaluating a suspicious transaction.


[Banks](https://www.alkami.com/banks/) and credit unions that stay relevant will be the ones that act as trusted partners and use data to deliver timely guidance and personalized insights. By being able to identify and automatically show up in the moment it matters, financial institutions can deepen product adoption and long-term loyalty.


While needs differ by generation, there’s a shared opportunity to make every digital interaction more relevant, useful, and worthy of the relationship.


### FAQs


1


What are generational banking trends?


Generational banking trends describe patterns in how different age groups approach digital banking, service, security, financial guidance, and relationship growth. They are most useful when combined with individual behavior rather than used as fixed labels.


2


How can a financial institution use AI across generations?


Start with a specific job to be done. AI can help explain a financial decision, surface a timely next step, or identify suspicious activity. The experience should make the value clear and give the account holder an understandable way to act.


3


What is the first digital experience a financial institution should improve?


Account opening is a strong place to begin because it is often the first meaningful test of clarity, safety, and ease for prospective account holders. Review the application journey across mobile and web, identify where applicants pause or abandon, and connect approval to the next useful action.
